I would keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the most familiar path for me, it fits the local water and weather, and at my age I want something steady, mechanized, and not too complicated. At the start of the season, my winter wheat is already in the field from last autumn, so I would manage that carefully through jointing and grain filling, then harvest it in early summer and plant summer maize right after. I would not spread myself across too many crops, because I care more about stable yield, simpler field work, and lower risk than chasing a little extra income from something harder to manage. Since you did not give a land size, I am treating my farm as 10 mu of main cropland and using the same 10 mu for winter wheat and then summer maize.
